summary: Verified A: INSERT...ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING genuinely raises no error for the losing row (Postgres speculative-insertion semantics; confirmed TypeORM InsertQueryBuilder.js line 330 emits the onConflict string verbatim after ON CONFLICT). B: arbiter target ('tenant_id', ((metadata ->> 'bullmq_job_id'))) WHERE (metadata ->> 'bullmq_job_id') IS NOT NULL is structurally/semantically identical to the migration's index expression after Postgres parse-time normalization of quoting/parenthesization (unquoted lowercase metadata == quoted "metadata"; extra parens are dropped); verified NotificationEntity column names match raw returning('*') keys used (saved.id, saved.created_at). C: walked the concurrent-insert interleaving against DatabaseContextService.runInTenantContext -- the losing INSERT blocks on the winner row lock until winner's transaction commits/rolls back, so the fallback SELECT in the same transaction reliably sees the committed winner row under READ COMMITTED; no poisoned-transaction risk since ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING never raises 23505. D: confirmed notifications.processor.spec.ts and dunning.service.spec.ts fully mock the query-builder chain (insert/into/values/onConflict/returning/execute) -- the raw SQL fragment is never exercised against real Postgres in CI; no e2e test found. Filed find-ae9be779 (LOW, residual gap, not a functional defect, per task framing). E: confirmed the concurrent MM changes to entities.ts (TransactionTipo->TransactionType, documentos->documents, enum renames) are unrelated pre-existing naming-normalization work that does not touch NotificationEntity or this path. Ran the three specified spec files: 3 suites / 36 tests passed. Attempted to construct failure scenarios for jobId undefined (insert always succeeds, never enters conflict path -- correct) and fallback SELECT returning null (winner rolls back after all / row deleted mid-race) -- both extremely low-probability edge cases, no worse than the prior implementation. No reproducible functional defect found in the new atomic ON CONFLICT mechanism.
